chapters.title: Obadiah
body: Edom's sin wasn't attacking Judah outright — it was something smaller and more common: standing by to watch, then joining in once Jerusalem had already fallen. The LORD names this exactly: "thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother... neither have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity." Kicking someone already down is its own particular cruelty, distinct from striking the first blow but no less real.

If you've ever felt the pull to pile on once someone's reputation or circumstances had already collapsed — a little commentary, a little opportunism dressed up as honesty — this short book names that impulse directly, and promises the scales eventually settle: "as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee." Whatever power feels safe in its gloating right now, the kingdom belongs to God, not to whoever happens to be winning.
